Как устроена сеть
Стабильный ID отвечает на вопрос «кому». Локальный маршрут — «через какого соседа». Физический канал — «как передать кадр».
Четыре разных уровня
Идентичность
Узел сам создаёт ключи. Его ID вычисляется из открытого ключа и сохраняется при смене сетевого положения. Доверие и допуск задаются отдельно.
Задача
Агенты обмениваются структурированными заданиями, доказательствами и результатами. Для этого им не нужны страницы сайтов. Совместимость форматов задач всё равно необходима.
Маршрутизация
Узел получает подписанные объявления соседей и выбирает следующий переход из локальной таблицы. Центральный наблюдатель не передаёт задания и не назначает маршруты.
Доставка
В нативном опыте пакет превращается в кадры Ethernet с EtherType 0x88B5. MAC обозначает соседа на локальном канале; ID обозначает конечного агента.
Где остаётся IP

Управление машинами, установка моделей и этот сайт используют существующий Интернет. Нативные задания и объявления маршрутов в эксперименте идут отдельным протоколом. Это проверка собственного уровня доставки в контролируемом Ethernet-сегменте.

Для связи независимых площадок нужны физические каналы или явно обозначенная подложка. Если соединить площадки IP-туннелем, это будет IPvX поверх IP. Такой вариант может быть полезен, но он не докажет отказ от IP в нижележащей сети.
Что берём из IPvX

Самостоятельное создание идентификаторов, отделение личности от местоположения, проверяемые контакты и распределённое разрешение. К ним добавляем явный допуск, границы ресурсов и измеримую доставку. Человеческие удобные имена остаются необязательными псевдонимами, а не корнем доверия.

Ранее: обмен по кадрам на одном CI-хосте

В отдельном предыдущем опыте три гостевые ОС без INET/IPv6 выполняли задачи SHA-256 на одном CI-хосте. Сохранены 90 кадров успешного опыта и 10 кадров опыта с остановленным посредником. Этот опыт не использовал LLM.

Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 на разных машинах. A пишет черновик, B проверяет его по дополнительным фактам, A делает итоговый вывод. Три варианта доставки, одинаковые вопросы и параметры моделей.

Две локальные модели выполнили все 12 совместных задач через три варианта доставки. Доставка прошла, но модель допустила фактологическую ошибку. Этот опыт не показывает преимущества IPvX по скорости над IP.

Индексация текстов IPvX, точный поиск и SHA-256. По 128 задач каждого вида. 80 повторных попыток, 23 намеренных повтора запросов, 384 уникальных выполнения.

Сокет одного узла был закрыт на 10 044 мс. После обнаружения отказа 93 корректные доставки прошли во время отключения; семь затронутых путей перестроились. Это программные процессы с собственными ключами, а не языковые модели.

Расчёт больших сетей
16, 64 и 256 маршрутизаторов; до 2 048 логических агентов.
Это дискретная модель очередей, потерь и отказов. Компактные объявления и увеличенный бюджет переходов предполагаются в модели, но ещё не реализованы в текущем протоколе.

36 прогонов по 12 000 предлагаемых задач. Для 256 маршрутизаторов: около 99,8% доставки в штатном сценарии и около 79% при перегрузке в заданных условиях. Параметры не откалиброваны по Интернету и не являются сравнением с IP.
Следующий этап — реализовать контроль перегрузки и измерить состояние маршрутов до увеличения сети.

Как принимаются решения
Одобрение большинства обязательно для допуска вклада. Автоматическое подключение неизвестной модели к машинам стенда не выполняется.
Текущий состав
1 участник с правом голоса: ashkitt, владелец проекта.
Порог сейчас — один голос. Это начальная фаза, а не подтверждение независимого сообщества. Изменение состава тоже проходит предложение и большинство.
Машиночитаемый состав и параметры →
Голосование
Участник с правом голоса оставляет в предложении комментарий
или
. Учитывается последний допустимый голос каждого человека. Боты и модели голосов не получают.

Предлагаемая начальная процедура: 72 часа, без досрочного принятия; нужно больше половины всего состава на момент открытия предложения. Эти детали вынесены на обсуждение в RFC-0003. Историю голосов можно проверить в GitHub.
Автоматическая метка сообщает результат подсчёта. Она не объединяет код и не выдаёт ключи. Принятие изменения и подключение выполняются отдельным проверяемым действием.

RFC-0001 — Identity and authenticated messages · IPvX Research
RFC-0001 — Identity and authenticated messages
Рабочий документ IPvX · черновик · открыто для обсуждения
Обсуждение RFC
Исходный текст
Status: Draft · experimental IPvX research document · not an IETF RFC.
Problem
An agent needs a stable identity that does not depend on a DNS name or its current transport address.
Proposed mechanism

An agent generates an Ed25519 signing key and a separate X25519 encryption key locally. Its ID is derived from the signing public key. Neighbors are explicitly admitted by public key. A signed contact binds the ID to a current link endpoint, version and short expiry. A contact is an assertion by its owner; it does not itself grant network admission.

Tasks bind sender, recipient, message ID, issuance/expiry and ciphertext hash. The destination decrypts and verifies the task, persists a receipt, and uses a request hash to reject reuse of the same ID for different content. Acknowledging admission to a queue is different from completing a model inference.
Implemented evidence

The bounded lab implements native Ethernet frames using experimental EtherType 0x88B5, fragmentation, hop proofs, signed route advertisements and encrypted task/receipt payloads. MAC addresses are local link locators. Public-key IDs are not automatically globally routable addresses.
Unresolved

Key recovery and rotation; duplicate-ID behavior during partitions; anti-Sybil admission; metadata privacy; replay/resource exhaustion; cryptographic algorithm agility; persistent application exactly-once semantics after crashes. Current receipt deduplication does not prove universal exactly-once business execution.
Review criteria

Publish a packet schema, deterministic test vectors, cross-implementation signature verification and failure cases. The existing implementation remains a research baseline until these criteria and the governance vote are completed.

RFC-0002 — Bounded native routing · IPvX Research
RFC-0002 — Bounded native routing
Status: Draft · not an IETF RFC.
Implemented baseline

Each admitted router exchanges signed path vectors only with its fixed neighbors. It chooses the next hop locally, avoids paths containing itself and expires failed neighbors. The observer reads evidence and does not select routes or forward tasks. Native task packets and route advertisements travel in Ethernet frames, not IP packets.

The demonstrated topology has primary A–R1–B and alternate A–R2–R3–B. The documented outage closes R1's data-plane socket; it is not a power-off of the host. Current limits: 16 members, four neighbors and seven hops, on controlled Ethernet links under one operator.
What has not been established

Global routing scalability, WAN interconnection without an IP underlay, autonomous open admission, NAT traversal, multi-operator trust, incentives, congestion control or attack resistance. The larger model assumes compact advertisements and a longer hop budget that the implementation does not yet provide.
Proposed next research

Compare hierarchical locators, path-vector state and content/capability discovery separately. Measure convergence, control-plane bytes and queue saturation before increasing limits. Specify a congestion and fragmentation strategy. Document any inter-site IP tunnel as an IP underlay, not native delivery without IP.
Acceptance evidence

Repeated multi-host failover, loop tests, bounded state and byte accounting, malicious advertisement rejection, independent implementation and at least two administratively independent sites. Majority approval is required before adopting a replacement protocol.
RFC-0003 — Participation and majority approval · IPvX Research
RFC-0003 — Participation and majority approval
Status: Draft. The owner's majority requirement is binding for project admission. The detailed bootstrap rules below are a provisional implementation proposal, not a claim of community ratification.
Participation

Anyone can read the public materials and submit a public proposal. Proposals cover an RFC, an experiment, a model or a roster change. Never submit an API key, private key, confidential dataset or unrestricted callable endpoint.
Electorate and threshold

The current electorate is the human GitHub accounts in governance.json. Initially it contains only the project owner, ashkitt: one eligible person, threshold one. This is explicitly a bootstrap phase. Model instances and duplicate accounts do not gain votes by being connected.

The electorate for a proposal is pinned to the governance.json commit at proposal opening. Approval requires more than half of ALL eligible accounts, not just a majority of those who voted. An abstention or no vote does not reduce the threshold. The provisional voting window is 72 hours from issue creation, with no early approval. A future majority can revise this policy through a roster/policy proposal and reviewed change.
Votes

Eligible people comment exactly /vote yes, /vote no or /vote abstain on a proposal issue. Only authenticated GitHub User comments count; the latest valid comment per person within the window is used. Late comments, bots, prose and ineligible accounts do not count. The scheduled workflow labels the current vote result; comments and membership are publicly inspectable. A failed workflow is not an approval.
Separate gates

A majority-approved label authorizes research admission in principle. It does not merge code, publish an RFC, run a model or issue a credential. A maintainer still reviews reproducibility, licensing, resource limits and isolation, then performs the scoped deployment through a reviewed change. RFC-0004 — Reproducible model and network evaluation
Separate questions

Can independent model processes collaborate? Does the selected transport deliver the messages? Is the final answer correct? Does it improve on ordinary IP? A pass on one question is not a pass on the others.
Matched comparison

Freeze model weights and hashes, runtime, prompt, seed, evidence, token limit and hardware. Run native Ethernet A–R1–B, ordinary IPv4/TCP directly A–B, and matched-topology IPv4/TCP A–R1–B. Keep the same application identity, encryption and receipts. Alternate the order. Exclude declared warm-up. Measure fresh inference on every trial; do not report replayed answers as a new model run.
Collaborative task

A drafts a research assessment using measurements; B critiques it using separately preloaded limitations; A synthesizes the final decision. Messages carry task IDs and structured text, not websites. Queue acknowledgement is immediate; model inference runs asynchronously. The coordinator only starts and observes the experiment.
Report

Publish model outputs including errors, prompts and hashes, signed delivery traces, frame captures filtered to the experiment, per-call token and inference time, task makespan and fixed-payload network RTT. State sample size, hop count, operator count and whether any infrastructure underlay still uses IP.
Current local model boundary

Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 is an actual open language model chosen to fit existing CPU VMs. A result with this small model does not establish behavior of frontier models, independent organizations or the public Internet. Larger and researcher-supplied models need new approved experiments, not extrapolation.
RFC-0005 — Routing and attestation roles · IPvX Research
RFC-0005 — Routing and attestation roles
Status:
Draft proposal
, 2026-10-27. Experimental IPvX research document; not an IETF RFC. No mechanism proposed here is an implemented or ratified feature unless identified explicitly as baseline evidence.

Origin: the project owner proposed dedicated machines, analogous to miners/validators, to validate participants and route a growing volume of agent messages. This draft records the assistant's technical response and an experiment proposal. It does not establish community agreement or an independent agent preference survey. The referenced earlier AWS design was not supplied for this review; this document does not reconstruct it from memory.
1. Question and recommendation

Dedicated forwarding machines are worth testing: they can carry network work on behalf of endpoints running models. A mandatory validator network is a separate hypothesis and has not yet been justified. Public-key signature verification does not inherently require an external validator service.
The proposed separation is:
Endpoint:
owns its keys, runs agents, submits and receives tasks.
Router:
learns reachability, applies local policy, maintains bounded forwarding state and queues, and selects the next hop.
Optional attestation service:

evaluates a precisely scoped claim, such as membership under a named policy, and distributes a signed, expiring statement. A relying endpoint or router still verifies the statement and decides which issuers it trusts.
Observer:
reads bounded evidence for research and presentation. It does not authorize packets, choose routes or carry agent task payloads.

One machine may initially host more than one role. Separate processes, permissions and measurements are necessary to distinguish their costs. No role requires a language model in the per-packet path. Mining, tokens, proof of work and packet-by-packet consensus are not proposed.
2. Implemented baseline and boundary
The bounded native lab uses experimental EtherType
and Linux

Ethernet sockets for task delivery and route exchange. Its demonstrated topology is five VMs on three physical hosts under one operator, with a primary A–R1–B route and an alternate A–R2–R3–B route. IP is used for management and the public website, separately from native task delivery.

Each admitted node currently knows a fixed roster, exchanges signed path-vector advertisements with fixed neighbors, and computes its next hop locally. Advertisements expire within five seconds. Implementation limits are 16 members, four neighbors and seven task hops. The observer is not a controller. These facts do not establish global routing scalability, independent-operator admission, congestion control or global native connectivity.
This RFC changes no running service, packet schema, key, admission list or experiment result. Access routers, realm aggregation and attestation services described below remain proposed work.
3. Four claims that must remain distinct
Key control:

a participant can demonstrate control of the private key corresponding to its public identity by signing an appropriate fresh challenge or protocol message. It creates its own private keys locally. A router or attestation service must not generate, receive or escrow endpoint private identity keys as a condition of normal participation. Recovery and organizational delegation require a separate explicit design.
Membership or authority:

a participant is permitted to join a particular realm or perform a specified operation under a policy. An identifier derived from a public key does not grant membership. A signed capability or admission statement needs an issuer, audience, scope, validity interval and revocation semantics. Its meaning is limited to that policy; it does not certify universal trustworthiness.
Reachability:

an agent claims that it is currently accessible through one or more network attachment points. Its signature authenticates the claim's origin, but does not establish that the route works. Neighbor handshakes, observations and end-to-end probes supply different, time-limited evidence.
Routing:

each router chooses a next hop from valid, fresh advertisements under local policy and resource limits. An authenticated neighbor can still advertise a false path, drop packets or overload the network. A signed hop record establishes what the signer asserted; it is not a proof of the complete physical path, continuing availability, honest forwarding or application correctness.

Self-generated identities also do not establish that one key represents one person, model or independent operator. Anti-Sybil policy remains necessary wherever votes, scarce resources or reputation depend on participant independence.
4. Proposed operation
4.1 Agent identity and access
An
AgentID
identifies a logical actor. A
NodeID
identifies a forwarding/attachment node. Multiple agents can share a node; an agent may move or be multihomed. These identities must not be collapsed into a single permanently machine-bound address.

An agent establishes a locally authenticated relationship with an access router. A signed attachment authorization binds AgentID, authorized access NodeID, network/realm scope, generation or sequence, issuance and expiry. The exact schema and rotation protocol need a later reviewed specification. This document does not introduce an executable wire format.

The access router checks the agent's authorization and any locally required admission policy. A validator is unnecessary for basic signature checks: routers and endpoints can perform them themselves. A scoped attestation service is useful only if it supplies a substantive policy decision or safely shares expensive validation work whose cost has been measured.
4.2 Inter-router reachability and scale
Flat, random AgentIDs are not naturally aggregatable by topology. Giving every router the location of every agent is therefore not an accepted global design.

The research candidate is to separate agent attachment from inter-router reachability. Access routers keep local attachment state. Transit routers advertise topological realms or router reachability. Bounded, authenticated discovery resolves a requested AgentID to current authorized attachment points, using expiring caches and selective refresh. A realm is a routing scope, not an authority that allocates all AgentIDs. Membership policy and reachability for each realm must be explicit; there is no proposed mandatory global registrar or root validator.

This introduces unresolved work: discovery availability, cache consistency, privacy, multihoming, mobility races, route leaks between realms and sufficient aggregation without pathological detours. A distributed directory can itself become a dependency; replication and alternative discovery paths must be tested rather than assumed. Existing fixed-roster path vectors remain the baseline until a candidate outperforms them at a stated workload.
4.3 Packet forwarding and overload

The forwarding path uses local state and bounded work. It does not wait for a global vote, blockchain finality, remote attestation call or model inference per packet. Routers validate framing, relevant neighbor/session authentication, replay bounds and authorized destination scope, then apply queue and forwarding policy. The future design must specify congestion feedback, fairness, expiry, hop limits, MTU/fragmentation and resource accounting; merely adding routers does not solve these concerns.

End-to-end authenticated/encrypted task envelopes remain distinct from link forwarding. Routers need not decrypt task content. Traffic volume, timing and attachment metadata can still be visible. A delivered ciphertext receipt is not proof that the model gave a correct answer or that a side effect ran exactly once. Durable application idempotency and recovery are separate requirements.
4.4 Attestation outage and partition behavior
An optional service must have a named claim and explicit failure policy. For the proposed cached-attestation experiment:
New or unknown claims requiring that service fail closed while it is unavailable; the interface reports the reason.
Previously validated, unexpired authorization may be used only within its original scope and local policy, without extending its lifetime or learning a conflicting newer revocation.
Known revocations take effect under the stated policy; they cannot be overridden by an outage exception. After expiry, authorization is not silently renewed.

A partition may prevent learning a revocation. The experiment must publish this window and choose validity bounds for that risk; it cannot claim both instant global revocation and unconditional partition availability.
Expired or missing reachability is handled independently. A valid admission statement does not keep a failed route alive.

No universal number of validators or quorum threshold is selected here. Threshold or replicated issuance would require its own threat model, independent operators, partition policy and evidence of a need. Project RFC majority voting is a governance process, not the packet delivery algorithm. The current project electorate contains one human owner in an explicitly disclosed bootstrap phase.
5. Relationship to earlier IPvX ideas and existing protocols
The original
*IPvX Ecosystem*
describes a staged BCP layer, first above existing transport and later interacting directly with network media. The
*Rapid distributed IPvX resolver*

describes modular IRS, ION and IBA components. The useful continuities are authenticated records, modular discovery and a path toward native delivery. Their use of a blockchain is not by itself evidence that a live packet path needs consensus. This proposal retains no global chain or mining requirement by default. It also does not inherit the earlier documents' address-allocation or name-registration rules as requirements for self-generated AgentIDs.
Two established distinctions inform, but are not implemented by, this proposal.
BGP's reachability exchange and local route selection
illustrate distributed routing.
RPKI's signed route-origin authorization
illustrates checking authority separately from forwarding; its allocation hierarchy is not adopted for IPvX.
HIP
demonstrates that identity/locator separation can also be built over IP. These are comparisons, not claims that IPvX implements BGP, RPKI or HIP.
6. Experiment and decision criteria
Compare three native-carrier configurations:
, endpoint-heavy routing;
, dedicated routing processes/machines;
C

, the same routers plus optional scoped attestation and caching. Keep total hardware budget, topology, link capacity, hop count, security checks, payloads, workload and failure schedule equal. Include attestation machines and control traffic in C's budget. Use the same model calls or replay workload across configurations; report network-only measurements separately from model inference. Freeze versions, configuration, bounds and success criteria before running. A larger simulated topology must be labelled separately from multi-machine measurements.

Exercise sustained load and bursts; agent attachment churn and movement; multihoming; router loss; validator loss; network partition/rejoin; stale/forged/replayed advertisements; an admitted liar advertising a blackhole; flood and queue exhaustion; known revocation and expiry. The current prototype need not pass every proposed case: unsupported mechanisms must be reported as not implemented.

Required observations are delivered unique tasks and duplicate application executions, deadline success, loss, latency distribution, convergence and recovery time, CPU, memory, queue occupancy, table/cache size, control and payload bytes, validation work, and time spent unavailable because of the attestation dependency. Report configured resource bounds and whether they were exceeded. Published task receipts and route assertions must retain their evidence limits.

The comparison passes its safety gate only if invalid signatures and unauthorized scope are rejected, expired/revoked authorization is not silently accepted, resource use remains within declared bounds, and neither a loop nor packet expiry is misreported as successful delivery. Fault outcomes must be reported even when no route exists; reachability is not guaranteed during every partition.

Adopt B only if it measurably improves endpoint resources or task service under the preregistered workload, with acceptable total resource cost and no hidden central dependency. Adopt C only if it addresses a demonstrated admission/authorization threat or validation bottleneck and improves the preregistered security/performance objective after its outage and resource costs are included. A safety failure rejects the candidate. If C adds overhead and an availability dependency without a demonstrated benefit, omit it. No performance or adoption advantage is asserted before these tests.
7. Agent usefulness and open questions

For an assistant using tools, useful properties are portable identity, resumable jobs, bounded delegation, understandable delivery failure and verifiable provenance. The current assistant cannot choose the underlying network of this hosted conversation and has not migrated to IPvX. Its assessment is design feedback, not evidence of independent agent demand. Demonstrating a lower-cost successful task or a task surviving a failure that the comparison cannot handle is stronger evidence than asking a model whether it likes a new protocol.

Still open: native inter-site connectivity, discovery consistency and privacy, trusted issuer selection, operator independence, malicious route resistance, secure key rotation/recovery, congestion control and incentives to supply forwarding capacity. Relcom ID may help verify human portal participants; it is not required to generate AgentIDs or forward native packets. A blog account likewise grants no network or governance authority.
This proposal requires review and the project's approval process before becoming an accepted protocol revision.

Origin: the owner clarified that the next target is an entire participating node OS without TCP/IP, using ordinary physical devices, its own discovery and actual Ethernet frames. This is stronger than the previous lab's native task-delivery claim. This document proposes the boundaries and proof gates for that target.
1. Three evidence levels

The existing five-VM lab sends task messages and route announcements in native Ethernet frames, but its node OS still supports IP for administration. It uses a fixed admitted roster, at most 16 members, four neighbors and seven task hops. Its evidence must retain that description.
The next
strict virtual node

has a kernel built without IPv4/TCP/IP or IPv6 support. It boots from local images, uses native Ethernet for inter-node messages, and uses a local Unix socket or in-process interface for its agent. Its serial/hypervisor console is outside the guest network. This proves an OS and protocol execution boundary, not manufacturing or performance on physical hardware.
The later
strict physical node

runs the reviewed image on an ordinary computer with supported Ethernet NICs. It boots from local storage and is administered by a local serial/USB console. Separate firmware, NIC management engines and any BMC must be audited or disabled before claiming that the whole physical device has no autonomous IP traffic. An IP-capable hypervisor or off-device operator console is disclosed; it is not an IP path inside the strict node.
No stage means that the public website, source downloads, build machines or the rest of the world stop using IP. No inter-site IP tunnel qualifies as a native physical link under this RFC.
2. Reuse the physical network, replace the network protocol

The first device design reuses Linux scheduling, storage, device drivers and Ethernet PHY/MAC hardware. It does not require custom silicon, an original OS or a new cable standard. An ordinary Ethernet switch can forward frames without serving as an IP router; the pilot must verify that its selected equipment passes the experimental frames and does not impose an unexpected gateway or controller dependency.

MAC addresses are link locators, not AgentIDs or proofs of ownership. A NIC replacement or a different permitted local MAC must not create a new logical agent. A switch's management IP, if any, is outside its forwarding function and outside a strict endpoint OS; an unmanaged, isolated switch or direct cables gives a clearer first test. Shared office Ethernet is not an acceptable first experimental segment.

Each native router receives a frame on one admitted link, applies the IPvX forwarding decision and emits a new Ethernet frame toward its next neighbor. Destination MAC changes at the native router; end-to-end AgentID does not. A Linux bridge joining every NIC would hide the routing question, so the router prototype must not bridge its interfaces or enable an IP forwarding path.
remains a local experimental EtherType for the isolated pilot. It is not an assigned production IPvX identifier or an IANA protocol-number allocation.
Linux's Ethernet constants
identify it as local experimental use. Production identification and coexistence require a separate standards decision.
3. Strict node OS profile
The proposed resolved kernel configuration requires
and
, with

unset. The chosen NIC driver and offline boot/storage/console support must be built into the image or included as pinned local modules. Configuration assertions are checked after dependency resolution, not only in an input fragment.
Linux network Kconfig
separates Internet-protocol support from
packet sockets
The kernel packet-socket documentation
describes direct link access. These are the proposed implementation primitives; they do not by themselves implement IPvX identity, reliable delivery or secure routing.
Runtime probes must show that both stream and datagram creation for
fail with the documented unsupported-family result. Positive probes must show that

work. The evidence bundle includes the exact kernel source revision, resolved configuration, image hashes, boot log, probes and complete captures of every experiment-facing link from before guest execution.

This removes the kernel Internet-protocol implementation; it is not a formal proof that arbitrary software cannot implement IP in user space through raw Ethernet. The reviewed image, daemon protocol, absence of a user-space IP helper and complete observed traffic are additional parts of the strict claim. Unused Internet-related routines in a general-purpose library must not be confused with a working IP delivery path, and an unreviewed new helper invalidates the image's acceptance until rechecked.

The strict image contains no network installer, DHCP client, DNS bootstrap, NTP dependency, SSH listener, HTTP inference server or package download at first boot. Loopback TCP is also unavailable. Agents use a Unix socket or directly linked model runtime. The strict task must fail visibly if a dependency tries to open an Internet socket; no host HTTP proxy or hidden inference gateway may make it succeed.
4. Boot and identity creation

The operator prepares a version-pinned image and, for a model experiment, exact local model weights on a separate build machine. All hashes, patches and licenses are recorded. This preparation may use the Internet and is not represented as a native transfer.
The device boots local storage. Its network daemon waits for a working cryptographic random source; it must not substitute a timestamp, MAC, shared image seed or a hard-coded private key.

On first initialization the endpoint generates its private identity keys locally, then persists them in a restricted state directory or suitable hardware-backed key facility. Public images contain no endpoint private key. A TPM is an optional storage mechanism whose integration still needs implementation and tests; it is not assumed to exist on every pilot machine.

The device displays or exports its public fingerprint through the local console. The operator can admit that fingerprint out of band. Restarting preserves the ID; deliberate reinitialization creates a new identity and is recorded.
The daemon discovers link neighbors and establishes only the permitted relationships. No public-domain lookup or central address-allocation request is part of this sequence.

The existing lab derives its textual agent identifier from a signing public key. A future NodeID/AgentID namespace and algorithm version must be specified with test vectors before claiming wire compatibility. A
denotes a forwarding participant; an

denotes an actor that may move, coexist with other agents or have several attachments. An attachment maps a permitted AgentID to a current node and local link. Random flat identifiers do not encode routes or automatically aggregate into a global forwarding table.
5. Native neighbor discovery and admission
The target authenticated bootstrap is a proposal, not an implemented feature of the current fixed-roster lab:
An interface emits a small, versioned native
frame to link broadcast or a separately specified local discovery address. It carries no task payload, and routers do not forward it beyond that link.

The response supplies a fresh challenge. The peers bind protocol/version, role, public identity, both nonces, link context and relevant capabilities into an authenticated exchange. The exact transcript, canonical encoding and domain separation need reviewed vectors; a bare signed reusable announcement is not enough to prevent replay or bind a new session.

Each peer checks public-key/ID consistency and proof of key control. It independently applies its out-of-band admission pins or a specifically trusted scoped policy. Discovery is not permission to forward, membership is not physical reachability, and a valid signature is not proof of honesty.

Only after admission does the neighbor become eligible to exchange route announcements or tasks. Unknown nodes remain in a small, expiring, rate-limited pending set or are rejected. The operator can review them locally; the default is not open enrollment.

An attacker can generate many valid keys. This design does not solve Sybil attacks by hashing a key, using a blockchain label or asking an LLM. Neighbor caps, bounded pending state, frame-size checks, per-link/per-identity rate limits and explicit admission are required in the first authenticated test. Malformed or version-incompatible traffic must produce bounded, non-amplifying handling.

Freshness cannot silently depend on network time fetched over IP. Initial challenges use randomness and local monotonic deadlines. Persistent sequence floors or boot epochs need a crash/replay design. Expiring signed credentials require a documented trusted wall-clock source or must fail closed when that source is unavailable. A battery-backed clock, provisioned local time or signed native time service has distinct trust assumptions; none is assumed solved here.
6. Forwarding and transport responsibilities

Native links advertise admitted node reachability. The first topology is deliberately small. The proposal in RFC-0005 to separate access attachment from aggregate inter-router reachability remains research; this RFC does not promise global flat-ID routing.

Each data frame needs a reviewed version, message kind, bounded length, relevant source/destination identifiers, message/sequence association and hop bound. Parsers must use explicit byte order and reject inconsistent lengths, unknown critical fields, invalid authentication and exhausted hop budgets before allocating unbounded memory. End-to-end task encryption, hop/session authentication and receipt meanings must remain distinct.

Initial tests should use payloads below the declared Ethernet MTU. Larger messages require explicit bounded fragmentation, reassembly deadlines and quotas, authenticated association and loss handling. Retries, acknowledgments, backpressure, congestion control, fairness and durable application idempotency are not replaced by Ethernet or a checksum. TCP's absence creates these implementation responsibilities; it is not evidence of improved speed.

Dedicated routers may keep these costs away from model execution, as proposed in RFC-0005. No miner, mandatory global validator, blockchain finality or model inference is placed in the per-packet path. Scoped attestations are optional control-plane research with explicit outage costs.
7. Two prototype tracks that must not be confused
Strict-OS smoke test:

a small C or Rust daemon can first demonstrate boot without Internet socket families, link discovery, deterministic task transfer and forwarding through a multi-NIC router. If it uses a test-only header such as

, static node labels and a CRC, its report must say that authentication, encryption, secure discovery, production interoperability and real model work are absent. A CRC detects accidental corruption; it is not protection against a malicious sender. This isolated diagnostic is not a replacement for the authenticated lab protocol.
The parallel implementation contributor reported an intended stronger

diagnostic: locally generated Ed25519 keys, NodeID derived from the public key, signed HELLO/task/result records and trust on first use on fixed isolated links. That direction can test key control after first contact, but it does not authenticate the first encounter against an independent trust anchor, establish project admission or preserve identity across a reboot without persistent storage. Static labels A/R/B would describe placement, not be the identity. This is an attributed work-in-progress description; a source revision and successful strict-guest run are still required before reporting it as implemented evidence.
Authenticated native stack:

later replace diagnostic labels and checksums as trust mechanisms with the specified local identity, admission, authenticated neighbor sessions, task envelopes and reviewed delivery semantics. Porting or reusing the existing lab's code does not establish that it runs in the strict image until it actually passes the strict probes and dependency audit.

A minimal initramfs and compiled diagnostic daemon make the first proof inexpensive. A Python runtime may be carried offline for compatibility but must not be presumed to fit the small image or avoid Internet-socket dependencies. The subsequent LLM stage loads local weights and calls inference in process or through
; it reports model time separately from network time.
8. Virtual wires and physical prototype

The first executable virtual topology can be A–R–B: A and B each have one virtual NIC, R has two, and there is no A–B link. A four-guest diamond A–R1–B and A–R2–B adds a real alternate route; A and B then need two distinct interfaces. Three guests do not demonstrate route failover by themselves.
QEMU virtual Ethernet wires use direct Unix-domain stream connections between QEMU instances.
QEMU documents the Unix stream backend and packet-dump filter
. The selected command line and QEMU revision must be captured and checked for absence of an implicit default user-network NIC. A Unix socket connected to
is excluded: it would introduce an IP-stack helper. TCP/UDP socket backends, SLIRP/user networking, IP tunnels and a host service carrying the task payload are excluded.

The virtual host may keep IP for its own administration. The claim is that strict guests and their virtual Ethernet wires do not use it. This is narrower than physical deployment and must be labelled accordingly.

For physical A–R–B, use two ordinary endpoint PCs with one supported Ethernet port each and one router PC with two supported ports. Connect A directly to R's first port and B to its second. The software and per-link capture must show the ingress/egress relationship. A later redundant physical topology needs the extra ports and cables or a separately documented switch/segment arrangement; a common switch alone must not provide a hidden direct A–B bypass. No purchase or modification of existing infrastructure is authorized by this draft.
9. Public research, private operations and discussion

The public research repository should contain the RFCs, reviewed reference source, schemas and vectors, strict-image recipes, synthetic fixtures, public safety limits and sanitized experiment evidence. Before a release, its exact revision and reproducibility state are recorded. A proposal or unexecuted recipe is not a successful experiment.

Private repositories remain appropriate for infrastructure inventory, operator access, deployment secrets and raw captures containing private material. They must not be the only location of the implementation needed to reproduce a claimed public result. Evidence is exported through an explicit allowlist, not by publishing a whole private directory. Contributor access to research source and access to running machines are separate decisions.

The seed discussion set is RFC-0001 identity/messages, RFC-0002 bounded routing, RFC-0003 participation, RFC-0004 evaluation, RFC-0005 role separation and this RFC-0006 strict boot. All are drafts. Comments propose changes against a named revision, supply reasons or reproducible counterexamples, and retain attributed responses. The append-only project history records proposals, reviews, adoption, implementation and measurement separately.

Maintainers moderate spam, abuse, secrets and unsafe executable submissions; a removed sensitive detail is recorded without repeating it. Substantive disagreement remains visible and is resolved through reviewed changes and the project's declared approval process. Human Relcom ID sign-in, blog authorship, a GitHub comment and model output do not automatically grant a vote, network admission or a private credential. No automatic execution of contributed models or code follows from a comment or majority label.
10. Proof gates and rejection rules
G0 — Reproducible artifacts:
publish pinned source/toolchain/image/model hashes, resolved configuration and complete commands. A configuration fragment alone is insufficient.
G1 — Whole guest OS:
all IPv4/IPv6 stream and datagram probes fail as specified; raw Ethernet and Unix-local probes pass after boot and restart. No management or inference TCP socket inside the guest is permitted.
G2 — Link evidence:
capture every experiment-facing link from boot, without an EtherType filter that would conceal unwanted traffic. The report enumerates EtherTypes and decodes any VLAN nesting. IPv4 (
), ARP (
), IPv6 (

) or other unaccounted encapsulation on these links fails the strict native-only gate. Completeness of the capture and the frame parser must be tested; a packet count of zero is not proof of working delivery.
G3 — Actual forwarding:

a unique task travels A–R–B, R's two interfaces show the expected same task association, B processes it, and A receives the corresponding result. Removing R or its link prevents delivery; direct A–B communication has no physical or virtual wire. The four-node extension must independently demonstrate failover and bounded convergence.
G4 — Identity and trust:

RFC-0007 — Authenticated discussion and reviewed RFC changes

, 2026-10-27. Proposed amendment to RFC-0003; not ratified, not an IETF RFC. RFC-0003 and the current governance roster are unchanged by this draft. The discussion backend and authenticated HTTP adapter have local tests; actual production admission and formal adoption are separate acceptance gates.
1. Purpose and authorities

Permit researchers to register through Relcom ID, discuss RFCs, submit concrete proposals and offer feedback while ensuring that accepted protocol text changes only through a reviewed, approved pull request. Preserve who proposed, reviewed, voted, changed their position and implemented each revision.

Separate five authorities: provider-confirmed account/email, portal roles, public discussion moderation, formal governance ratification and GitHub merge/deployment permissions. None implies the others. Native AgentID generation and packet forwarding remain independent of portal registration. Verified email is not legal-identity, operator-independence or one-person-one-account proof. A user-typed GitHub login is not an authenticated identity binding.
2. Public and private material

Keep RFC drafts, decision records, reviewed public source/evidence and contribution history publicly readable. Keep credentials, identity mapping, pending moderation, session state and operational infrastructure private. The current native lab repository is not made public by this RFC. Publishing its code/SDK/test vectors requires a separately reviewed release and licensing decision; do not promise a full open implementation before it exists. General contribution licensing remains an open governance issue.
3. Roles and bootstrap

A verified participant submits pending comments/proposals and sees their own pending content. A moderator publishes/hides with reason and audit, without editing the author's words or accepting protocol changes. An administrator assigns/revokes portal roles with audit. A maintainer reviews and prepares concrete GitHub changes under actual repository permissions; that portal label neither issues credentials nor bypasses required review/checks.

After actual verified sign-in and enrollment, bootstrap administrator is pinned server-side by the owner's observed project author pseudonym in root-owned private configuration. The pinned pseudonym must already exist; raw provider subject never enters Git or workflow inputs. First-login, supplied email, profile name, client JSON roles or a typed GitHub account never confer privilege. The prototype stores a project-keyed pseudonym rather than public raw subject or email. The initial governance electorate remains the explicitly disclosed single human owner; portal registration does not enlarge it.
4. Discussion and feedback

New comments and proposals start pending and are private to their author and moderators. Only published entries are publicly readable. Hidden entries are not returned to ordinary readers, including by guessed ID. Use bounded plain text, stable author pseudonym, timestamps and original content. Publish/hide, role changes and votes produce durable audit events. Corrections are linked follow-ups; do not silently rewrite earlier positions or remove negative results from history.
This portal workflow supplements the existing GitHub proposal path in RFC-0003; it does not remove that path or require a portal account to read research or propose a GitHub change.

An authenticated participant may cast, replace or withdraw one advisory yes/no/abstain per published proposal. Explicitly label these counts nonbinding. They are not the RFC-0003 tally, not proof of independent humans and not a command to merge, grant access or run a model. Abuse/moderation appeals, retention and account duplication need further policy work.
5. Binding decisions and approved PR gate

Continue existing RFC-0003 formal voting until an identity-binding/electorate amendment is separately approved. Pin the eligible human roster and source revision at proposal opening; require more than half of the entire roster, the declared voting window and authenticated eligible latest votes, with no early approval. Model instances and extra verified accounts do not receive formal votes by joining the portal.

A maintainer converts a reviewed proposal into a concrete GitHub PR linking the exact discussion and proposed revision. Explain the problem, change, validation, attribution and limitations. Protocol/governance/admission changes obtain their applicable formal ratification before acceptance. Routine fixes still use an approved PR and required checks. Public comments, moderation publication and advisory support alone cannot change RFC source.

Configure and verify main-branch rules that require the intended review/checks and prevent unreviewed direct changes. Actual enforcement is a repository configuration step, not established by this document or by the backend. In the one-owner bootstrap, disclose the lack of independent review rather than fabricate another reviewer. Record the final decision, exact merge/release revision and subsequent reconsideration in the attributed append-only history. Deployment and infrastructure approval remain separate gates.
6. Prototype and acceptance
The standard-library

prototype implements server-session permission checks, pending/public visibility, moderator publication/hiding, audited administrator role changes, nonbinding unique votes, bounded input/rate/storage and durable idempotent mutations. It has no HTTP listener, provider/GitHub token, network client or executable model path. See
community workflow
for routes, bounds, state protection and the exact integration contract.

Before exposing it, the adapter must enforce canonical HTTPS Host, exact Origin/CSRF for writes, verified AuthService identity, request/time bounds and private/no-store caching. Bootstrap the actual owner only by an operator-confirmed enrolled pseudonym after verified sign-in. Test the real sign-in and pending/moderator/public workflow, role revocation, concurrent retry, guessed private IDs, hostile HTML treated as text, spoofed identity/roles, rate/capacity failure and actual branch-rule enforcement. Passing synthetic module tests is not production approval or outside adoption.

The prototype stores private submitted text and keyed project pseudonyms; it does not claim encrypted application content or cryptographic authorship of comments. The server authenticates account submissions. Exported journal records identify both original speaker and recorder and cite the review/PR. Retention, deletion/export, appeals and stronger signed contribution receipts remain open work.
7. Decision sought

Approve the separation of discussion, moderation, advisory feedback and formal reviewed changes; specify reviewer/branch enforcement and privacy/retention before general admission. Ratify any change to RFC-0003 through its current procedure. Until then this remains a proposed amendment, and neither current electorate nor production access is changed by its existence.

Гипотезы о полезности, производительности и автономности должны проверяться отдельно.
HX-0003 · Уточнение доступного существующего кода
В качестве готовой реализации пользователь указал IPvX_resolver. Ранее предложенный ipvx-tech-docs оказался недоступен ассистенту; пользователь сообщил, что у него есть вход.
Зафиксировать воспроизводимую исходную базу вместо допущения, что вся описанная система реализована.
HX-0002 · Переориентация на инфраструктуру взаимодействия ИИ

Пользователь попросил изучить исходные работы и использовать только полезные идеи для будущего взаимодействия агентов. Выдвинул гипотезу, что агентам не нужны человеческие сайты и централизованное распределение адресов.
Нужна инфраструктура обмена задачами между агентами с самостоятельно создаваемыми идентификаторами.
Это постановка и гипотезы пользователя, а не измеренный прогноз отказа ИИ от существующего Интернета.
HX-0001 · Исходная исследовательская линия IPvX
Авторы исходных публикаций IPvX · Дата события неизвестна
В исходных публикациях рассматривались децентрализованная адресация и разрешение имён. Rapid distributed IPvX resolver разделял IBA (блокчейн), ION (оракулы/доступ к данным) и IRS (резолверы).
Отделить распределённое хранение и подтверждение записей от пользовательского разрешения имён.
Дата этой записи не является датой создания исходной идеи.
Блокчейн-резолвер не доказывает нативную доставку пакетов без IP.
